newsitem.title: USA: TCI satellite sale contested - Variety.
newsitem.headline: TCI satellite sale contested - Variety.

text.p: Tele-Communications Inc's plan to start a new joint-venture satellite television service has been contested by Time Warner Inc and other cable operators who allege TCI does not own satellites it agreed to sell as part of the deal, Daily Variety reported Tuesday.
TCI's joint venture is with Telesat Canada. Telesat is co-owned by Alouette Telecommunications Ltd, itself 57-percent owned by BCE Inc, Spar Aerospace Ltd, and other companies.

Variety said the details of the dispute were included in a filing with Securities & Exchange Commission just made by TCI Satellite Entertainment Inc, a new public company being formed by TCI to hold its satellite interests.
The value of the new company is likely to be affected by the outcome of the dispute, Variety said.

TCI said in the filing the dispute began in February when it advised Primestar Partners that Primestar had failed to "effectively exercise" an option to buy from TCI two satellites under construction.
Under a 1990 agreement, TCI gave Primestar an option to buy the satellites TCI was building if Primestar funded the $500 million construction cost.

According to Variety, TCI owns 20.86 percent of Primestar, while Time Warner Inc owns 31.2 percent. Cox Communications, Comcast Corp and Continental Cable each own about 10.4 percent. The remaining 16 percent is owned by General Electric Co.
Primestar subsequently agreed to the financing and had advanced $386.2 million toward the construction by June 30, the filing said, according to Variety.
TCI said in the filing it would repay the advances and sell the satellites to Telesat, pending government approval, for a price equal to the construction cost, Variety said.
The daily trade paper quoted a TCI spokeswoman as saying the dispute had not been resolved and "nothing has changed."
